solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They are customary items of clothing

definitions.meaning: the things a person customarily does
a habit is a monk's or nun's robe, or a riding outfit

explanation.surface: A remark that certain garments are traditional wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits are routine practices, and also the long robes worn by members of religious orders.

clue.text: Female has to stop outside, one joining me for rest period?

indicators.note: the word for stop sits outside, wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: to halt is to stop
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman must cease, with someone joining the speaker for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts HALT round F, giving HALFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-time is the interval between the two halves of a match, when players rest.

clue.text: Flourish as British operator heading off

indicators.note: the word's head, its first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a surgeon carries out operations

explanation.surface: Praise for a British doctor's success, said as the doctor leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the S from SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or thrive rapidly, so it means to flourish.

clue.text: With minimal underwear Georgia gets brown on top

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A woman named Georgia, in skimpy briefs, tans her upper body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' works because this is a down entry: the brown piece stands above the state in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a pair of very brief bikini-style knickers joined at the sides by strings.

clue.text: Criminal present with hidden aim

indicators.note: one word is said to hold another concealed within it, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: to present something is to offer it
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker offers a gift while concealing an ulterior motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as a gift, but here it is the verb, to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who has broken the law, a straightforward synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Mysterious object at rest in bumpy surface

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other
something bumpy is uneven and disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: lying means at rest, reclining

explanation.surface: Something strange is lying still on rough ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' makes FSAUCER, and the container lands after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying saucer is a supposed alien craft, the classic unidentified flying object.

clue.text: Grotesque doormen at entrances to public houses — no skinny type wanted!

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
entrances are the starts of words, so the first letters are taken

explanation.surface: Ugly bouncers on pub doors, where lean customers are not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotesque' rearranges DOORMEN into ENDOMOR; PH comes from the first letters of public houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An endomorph is a person with a rounded, heavy build, the opposite of a slim type.

clue.text: Persist in desperate attempt to get entrance secured finally, that is

parts.note: a door is an entrance

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word secured

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying hard to get a doorway locked at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Do or die names an all-out effort where one must succeed or perish, a desperate try.

clue.text: Game's 50-style male became tarnished

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game, plus the S of the possessive
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a young man dressed in 1950s Edwardian-revival style

explanation.surface: A sporting man's fifties look has lost its shine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a British youth of the 1950s who wore drape jackets and drainpipe trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusted means corroded by oxidation, a way metal becomes dulled and discoloured.

clue.text: Attracting lady initially with superior token of love

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word lady

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior
a ring is given as a pledge of love

explanation.surface: Wooing a woman by offering a fine love token.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'superior' (upper class) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring means enticing or drawing someone in, which is a form of attracting them.

clue.text: Medicine could be provided by ''doper'', yes?

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow could be rearranged to supply the answer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drug user might supply a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be provided by' signals rearranging DOPER and YES together into EYEDROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-drops are a liquid treatment dripped into the eye, a form of medication.

clue.text: A hotpot's made specially — eat it for lunch?

definitions.text: A hotpot's made specially — eat it for lunch?

indicators.note: specially made means put together in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-pot stew has been prepared specially for someone's lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges A HOTPOT'S MADE; the whole clue also describes the dish, a potato topping as on a hotpot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato is a dish of boiled potatoes pounded smooth, often served at a midday meal.

clue.text: After all, the poor horse may need a home

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
in means at home

explanation.surface: A broken-down horse may need somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Then again is a phrase introducing a contrary thought, much like on the other hand or after all.

clue.text: Girl departs, transported by wise man

indicators.note: one piece is carried within another, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a mage is a magus, a learned wise man
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A young woman leaves, carried off by a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported by' puts D inside MAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madge is a pet form of the female name Margaret.

clue.text: Tom, Dick or Harry entertains them with playing

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of the words given rearranges them

explanation.surface: An ordinary fellow amuses some people with his music or games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals rearranging ENTERTAINS THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick or Harry stands for any ordinary person, the average citizen.

clue.text: No festival to be without minimum of rain and wind

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the other pieces surround the letter

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, a single opening letter

explanation.surface: A wish for no celebration, and then a dry gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'; the entry is often written with an apostrophe, nor'easter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong wind blowing from the north-east.

clue.text: Bits of metal chaps found in that cheese

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other
bits of a word are its letters broken up and reassembled

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fragments of metal and some men turn up inside a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits of' makes EMTAL, split after its second letter to take the chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with large holes, one particular kind.

clue.text: Something hallucinogenic changing mood — charms user

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug that alters one's state of mind delights whoever takes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' signals rearranging MOOD CHARMS USER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred mushrooms are psilocybin fungi eaten in rituals for their mind-altering effects.

clue.text: Port given new part after redevelopment

indicators.note: redeveloped letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A harbour gains a fresh section once it is rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a link; 'after redevelopment' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's largest seaports.

clue.text: Vehicle I'm on, falling apart and almost beyond repair?

indicators.note: the letters fall apart and are reassembled in another order
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: bust means broken beyond repair

explanation.surface: A passenger complains the decrepit transport they ride is nearly wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling apart' rearranges I'M ON to OMNI; 'almost' trims BUST to BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full old name for a bus, a public road vehicle.

clue.text: More than one politician of eminence is visible round England's capital

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

indicators.note: the word is goes round the other letter, holding it inside
a capital is a word's head letter, its first

explanation.surface: A distinguished politician appears around the nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E (England's 'capital', its first letter) inside IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party, a group of politicians.

clue.text: Seaman reaches island to the west to find harbour

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives at an island and looks for a port on its western side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' means reading leftwards in an across entry; an ait (or eyot) is a Thames-style river islet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the seaport serving ancient Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Respect and honour is given to forefather, not half!

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the front four of its eight letters

parts.note: an ancestor is a forefather

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a forebear being shown great deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' keeps the first half of ANCESTOR, ANCE; it also reads as the British exclamation meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deference such as a bow, a show of respect.

clue.text: Area in Bath, say, overlooking church

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece looks down over the second from above

parts.note: Bath is an English spa town, an example of a spa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A district of the city of Bath that looks out over a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city famed for its Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: Space means an extent or expanse of room, an area.

clue.text: Angriest drunk appearing? One doesn't react

indicators.note: a drunken word staggers out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone appears furious when intoxicated, yet another stays unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals rearranging ANGRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert gas, such as neon or argon, hardly forms chemical compounds, so it does not react.

clue.text: A little something attached to leg that may prove advantageous

definitions.text: A little something attached to leg that may prove advantageous

parts.words: A little something attached to leg that may prove advantageous
parts.note: a lucky charm is the foot of this animal, attached at the end of its leg

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the lucky rabbit's foot: the animal is identified by the charm that hangs from its leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit's foot is carried for good luck, so the animal is known for this advantageous charm.

clue.text: Rise up in revolution with soldiers of higher quality

indicators.note: letters in revolution are overturned and thrown into a new order

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A call to rebel, joined by troops, to make something better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges RISE UP into SUPERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior describes something better or finer than others, of a higher standard.

clue.text: Something prickly Guy found by lake

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A man called Guy discovers something spiny beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a plant with spiny flower heads once used to raise the nap on cloth.
